title: Citations and answer formatting
summary: Citations tie each claim to the source text it came from. They prove provenance, not correctness, so a good design adds span-level pointers, a verification step and a UI that lets users check.
useIf: Answers must be traceable for trust, audit or compliance, or users need to verify claims quickly.
avoidIf: You would treat the presence of a citation as proof that the answer is supported.

explain.md: Three levels of citation exist. **Document level** names the file. **Chunk level** points to the retrieved passage. **Span level** points to the exact sentence or character range that supports a claim. Finer is more useful and harder to get right.

explain.caption: How citations are produced
head: Approach
How it works
Notes from the sources
rows: Label chunks `[1]`, `[2]` in the prompt and ask the model to cite them
Works anywhere, model can mis-cite or invent ids, so verify
Enable `citations` on `document` or `search_result` blocks. Types include `char_location`, `page_location` and `content_block_location`
`cited_text` does not count toward output tokens. Works with prompt caching, token counting and batch. Incompatible with structured outputs: enabling both returns HTTP 400 [[r27]]
Indexed sources can return service-made citation URLs (preview). Remote sources have no backing index and no citation URLs [[r6]]

explain.md: **A citation proves provenance, not entailment.** The cited span may not support the claim. ALCE, a benchmark for LLM answers with citations, found that on the ELI5 dataset even the best models lacked complete citation support 50% of the time [[tr10]]. Verify with an entailment (NLI) check or an LLM judge on each claim-span pair, or have the model **quote first**: for documents over 20k tokens Anthropic advises asking for word-for-word quotes before answering, and giving explicit permission to say 'I don't know' [[r41]].

steps.title: Number the evidence
steps.md: Give each chunk a stable id and metadata (title, page, URL).

steps.title: Answer with spans
steps.md: Ask for claims that name chunk ids, or use native citations.

steps.title: Verify
steps.md: Check each claim against its span. Drop or flag unsupported claims.

steps.title: Render
steps.md: Show inline markers, hover previews and a link to the source location.

explain.title: Format and citation features can conflict
explain.md: If you need schema-validated JSON and native citations from the same provider call, check compatibility first. Anthropic returns HTTP 400 when citations and structured outputs are both on [[r27]]. A common workaround is two calls, or prompt-based ids inside your schema (author suggestion).

whereToUse: Policy and compliance assistants where each statement needs a source page
Research and legal tools where users read the cited span before trusting an answer
Customer support answers that link to the article section used
Evaluation pipelines that score citation precision and recall automatically

use: Users or auditors must trace claims to sources
You can store chunk ids, page numbers and URLs as metadata
You can add a verification step for high-risk claims
The UI can show the cited span
avoid: Treating any citation as proof of support
Chunk metadata is missing, so links cannot point anywhere
Structured output is required and your provider cannot combine it with native citations
flips: Risk is high: add per-claim entailment checks and require quotes first
Latency is tight: cite at chunk level and verify only a sample
Documents are long: prefer span-level citations over whole-document links

pitfalls.symptom: A citation points to a passage that does not say what the answer claims
pitfalls.cause: The model cites by plausibility, and nothing checks entailment [[tr10]]
pitfalls.fix: Verify each claim against its cited span, and flag or remove unsupported claims

pitfalls.cause: Chunk ids or page offsets changed
pitfalls.fix: Use stable ids and store source URL, page and offsets as metadata

pitfalls.symptom: Request fails with HTTP 400 when enabling citations
pitfalls.cause: Native citations were combined with structured outputs on a provider that forbids it
pitfalls.fix: Split into two calls or move citation ids into your own schema

scenarios.title: Legal research with reviewer sign-off
scenarios.situation: Lawyers review AI-drafted summaries of case documents. Every statement must be checkable against a specific passage, and mistakes carry legal risk.
unknowns: Is native span citation available on the chosen provider?
scenarios.question: How do you design citations?

options.name: Span-level citations with quote-first prompting and an automated entailment check that flags unsupported claims for the reviewer
options.why: Provenance alone is not enough in a high-risk setting, and quotes plus a check catch mis-citation [[r41]] [[tr10]].
options.tradeoff: More tokens, latency and a verifier to maintain.

options.name: A source link at the end of each answer
options.why: The reviewer cannot tell which sentence came from which passage.

options.name: Chunk-level citations without verification
options.why: Cheaper and still traceable to a passage.

flips.if: Risk is low and speed matters
flips.then: Use chunk-level links and sample-based checks.

flips.if: Reviewers cannot open source documents from the UI
flips.then: Show the quoted passage inline next to each claim so the check does not depend on a click-through.

scenarios.takeaway: Risk sets how much you verify.

scenarios.title: Typed JSON answers plus citations
scenarios.situation: A claims-processing service needs schema-valid JSON output and a citation for each field value. The provider's native citation feature is under evaluation.
unknowns: Can the provider combine citations and structured output?
Is a second verification call affordable?
scenarios.question: What do you build?

options.name: Put chunk ids inside your schema (per-field `source_id` and `quote`), then verify the quote exists in the cited chunk with code
options.why: It works whichever provider restricts combining native citations with structured output [[r27]], and a string match on the quote is a cheap verifier.
options.tradeoff: You maintain prompt and schema, and quotes can still paraphrase, so allow a fuzzy match.

options.name: Enable native citations and structured outputs together
options.why: Anthropic returns HTTP 400 when both are on [[r27]].
options.tradeoff: Right if your provider documents that the combination is supported.

options.name: Two calls: structured extraction, then a separate citation call
options.tradeoff: Doubles calls and the second call can disagree with the first.

flips.if: The provider later supports both together
flips.then: Switch to native citations and drop the custom verifier for spans.

flips.if: The schema is relaxed to free text with inline citations
flips.then: Use the provider's native citations directly and sample-check them.

scenarios.takeaway: Check feature compatibility before designing the output.

quiz.q: A model cites chunk 3 for a claim, and chunk 3 does not support it. What does this show?
options: A citation proves provenance, not entailment, so supports need checking
quiz.explain: A pointer to a source does not show the source supports the claim. Verify with NLI, quote-first or a judge. ALCE found incomplete citation support about half the time on ELI5 for the best models [[tr10]].

quiz.q: A service enables Anthropic `citations` and a JSON schema output in one request and gets HTTP 400. What is the cause?
options: Citations are incompatible with structured outputs
quiz.explain: Enabling both returns HTTP 400. Prompt caching, token counting and batch are compatible with citations [[r27]].

quiz.q: Put a cite-then-check flow in order.
items: Generate claims that name chunk ids
Verify each claim against its span
Render markers with links to the source
quiz.explain: You need stable ids before generation, verification after generation, and rendering last so the UI shows only checked claims.

flashcards.front: Citation versus entailment: what is the difference?
flashcards.back: A citation shows where a claim came from. Entailment shows the source actually supports it. Check it separately.

flashcards.front: What is the incompatibility in Anthropic's Citations feature?
flashcards.back: Citations cannot be combined with structured outputs. Enabling both returns HTTP 400.

flashcards.front: What does OpenAI file search return for citations?
flashcards.back: `file_citation` annotations on the answer. Raw hits need `include: ["file_search_call.results"]`.
